text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hassan to open autumn session of parliament on Friday.
- World Food Programme said it would keep aid to Moroccan canteens after government promised to bring to court officials charged with embezzlement of donations.
- President of Parliament Jalal Essaid says Morocco enjoys privileged relations with France's legislative institutions.
- Education Minister Rachid Ben Mukhtar says education is in crisis and not adapted to the country's needs.
- Rabat and Madrid to approach European Union for backing for a tunnel linking Morocco and Spain.
- Appeal of pharmacist sentenced to nine years imprisonment for selling contaminated blood products postponed to Dec 10.
- State-owned Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) reinforces its policy of international networks through joint ventures.
- International Monetary Fund says need to combat corruption in recipient countries.
- Unions warn government against delay in implementing accord of August over social benefits.
